core_obligations: Prove (1) by comparing the map K[[y_1, ..., y_n]] to A with its reductions modulo all powers of the maximal ideal, which are isomorphisms, and using completeness of both rings (proof lines 9754-9758).

Prove (2) by extending the partial regular system of parameters to a full one, applying (1) to the completed system and identifying the quotient of the resulting power series ring by the chosen part (proof lines 9759-9764).
Obtain (3) and (4) by the same two arguments with the Cohen ring Lambda in place of the field K and the system starting with p (proof lines 9765-9766).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 9736-9766. The nearest records are 344 (9435-9528, tag 0DYG, testing formal smoothness by small Artinian extensions) and 343 (9256-9320, tag 07NJ, continuous lifting through closed topologically nilpotent ideals), both from the same block on complete local rings but about formal smoothness and lifting, not about presenting a power series ring from a regular system of parameters.
difficulty_reason: The lemma records the four standard consequences of choosing a regular system of parameters in a power series ring, once over a field and once over a Cohen ring: any two such systems present the ring as a power series ring on the system, any part of a system can be completed and the quotient is again a power series ring over the same base, and the same two statements hold for the system starting with p over a Cohen ring (statement lines 9736-9751). The proof is a 13-line argument (proof lines 9754-9766) which for (1) compares the two complete local rings by the surjections on the quotients by powers of the maximal ideal, for (2) extends the given partial system to a full one and reduces to (1), and then declares for (3) and (4) that the proofs are exactly the same. The decisive step is the passage from the identification of all the infinitesimal quotients to an isomorphism of complete rings, which is the completeness hypothesis doing real work; the author states it in one sentence and leaves the rest of the (3) and (4) cases by symmetry.
